name: gqa
reference:
import math

import torch

REFERENCE_ROWS = 256


@torch.inference_mode()
def run(q, k, v):
    batch, sequence, q_heads, head_dim = q.shape
    kv_heads = k.shape[2]
    assert q_heads % kv_heads == 0
    assert k.shape == v.shape == (batch, sequence, kv_heads, head_dim)
    assert q.dtype == k.dtype == v.dtype == torch.bfloat16

    # Expand head indices explicitly; row chunks bound reference memory.
    groups = torch.arange(q_heads, device=q.device) // (q_heads // kv_heads)
    queries = q.transpose(1, 2).float()
    keys = k.transpose(1, 2).float().index_select(1, groups)
    values = v.transpose(1, 2).float().index_select(1, groups)
    output = torch.empty_like(q)
    key_positions = torch.arange(sequence, device=q.device)
    scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(head_dim)

    # The oracle uses full FP32 products, softmax, and value accumulation.
    previous_tf32 = torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32
    torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False
    try:
        for start in range(0, sequence, REFERENCE_ROWS):
            stop = min(start + REFERENCE_ROWS, sequence)
            scores = torch.matmul(queries[:, :, start:stop], keys.transpose(-1, -2))
            scores.mul_(scale)
            query_positions = torch.arange(start, stop, device=q.device)
            scores.masked_fill_(key_positions[None, :] > query_positions[:, None], -torch.inf)
            weights = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
            result = torch.matmul(weights, values)
            output[:, start:stop] = result.transpose(1, 2).to(q.dtype)
    finally:
        torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = previous_tf32

    return output
